name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Democrat raised only ~$34k with minimal cash
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, Smith's decades-long incumbency, and the challenger's negligible fundraising all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets price the race around 96% Republican. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge or unexpected Smith scandal would be the main way this could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 14 points toward the GOP. Chris Smith, one of the longest-serving members of the House, is seeking another term and has the advantages of incumbency and name recognition built over decades in office.

His Democratic challenger, Rachel Peace, has raised only about $34,000 and had roughly $5,000 on hand, leaving her badly outmatched financially. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Smith about a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals all point to a comfortable Republican victory, with only a modest Democratic tail risk from the national environment.
